title: Which five numbers are more than one and less than another?
description: Farhan draws raffle tickets at a school fair, and a winning ticket must lie between two limits. The video writes five winning numbers by choosing the hundreds.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number more than one limit and less than the other must stay between both. Watch for a number that passes the low limit but is above the high limit.

source: Let Us Do (second set) 2, more than and less than
video_script.why: The child can name numbers between two numbers but may check only one end.
video_script.substitution: Keep the shared thirty-eight thousand, pick hundreds that stay above the low limit and below the high limit, and check both ends.
video_script.anchor: Farhan drawing raffle tickets at the school fair with a low and a high limit
video_script.wrong_answer: thirty-eight thousand, six hundred and fifty
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu picks thirty-eight thousand, six hundred and fifty because it is more than the low limit. He forgets that it is also above the high limit.

final_answer.spoken: thirty-eight thousand two hundred, three hundred, four hundred, five hundred and five hundred and ninety-nine

maths_rules: low limit 38,125 and high limit 38,600; both start with 38 thousand
the hundreds digit of the low limit is 1 and of the high limit is 6
slip: 38,650 > 38,600, so it is above the high limit
video_script.design: Exercise: five numbers above one limit and below another. Hint: the hundreds decide. The raffle drum with two limit signs stays as the anchor.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='fair'/>Farhan is drawing raffle tickets at the school fair. A winning ticket must be more than thirty-eight thousand, one hundred and twenty-five.
<bookmark mark='less'/>It must also be less than thirty-eight thousand, six hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write five winning ticket numbers.

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: a line from 38,125 to 38,600; the 38 thousand part glows; the hundreds digits 1 and 6 light up; the five empty tickets pulse

marks.same: the 38 thousand part of both limits glows
marks.hund: the hundreds digits 1 and 6 light up

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Both limits start with thirty-eight thousand. Only the last three digits can change.
<bookmark mark='hund'/>Look at the hundreds. The low limit has one hundred, and the high limit has six hundred.
<bookmark mark='try'/>A winning number has to stay above the low limit and below the high limit. Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 38,650; 38,650 is placed on the line right of the high limit; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.high: 38,650 is placed on the line to the right of the high limit
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Thirty-eight thousand, six hundred and fifty is more than the low limit, so it wins.
<bookmark mark='high'/>It is also more than the high limit.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>A winning number must be below thirty-eight thousand, six hundred as well.

beats.on_screen: the hundreds digits 2 to 5 light up; 38,200 and 38,500 are placed on the line

marks.try: the hundreds digits 2 to 5 light up

narration: <bookmark mark='try'/>Try hundreds from two to five.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Thirty-eight thousand, two hundred is more than the low limit.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Thirty-eight thousand, five hundred is less than the high limit.

marks.last: 38,599 appears just left of the high limit

narration: <bookmark mark='more'/>Thirty-eight thousand, three hundred and thirty-eight thousand, four hundred fit as well.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Thirty-eight thousand, five hundred and ninety-nine fits too, because it is only one below the high limit.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>These five numbers all fit, and many other answers are right.

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp'/>To check, read each number against both limits.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>It must be bigger than the low limit and smaller than the high limit.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Look at your five numbers. Is each one above the low limit and below the high limit?
